g1.label: 1. Rosa Parks refused to give up her seat on a ___
g1.why: She refused to give up her seat on a Montgomery bus in 1955.

g2.label: 2. King believed change should come through ___
g2.why: King argued for nonviolent protest as the way to change.

g3.label: 3. 'I Have a Dream' was delivered in ___
g3.why: The speech was given at the March on Washington in 1963.

g4.label: 4. Malcolm X: defend themselves ___
g4.why: He argued for self-defence 'by any means necessary'.

g5.label: 5. Malcolm X focused on Black pride and ___
g5.why: His emphasis was on Black pride and independence.

g6.label: 6. Both leaders were ___
g6.why: The text says both King and Malcolm X were assassinated.

g1.label: 1. King preferred peaceful protest. ___
g1.why: 'However' opens a new sentence to signal a contrast with what came before.

g2.label: 2. King focused on white America, ___
g2.why: 'Whereas' joins two clauses that contrast directly with each other.

g3.label: 3. Some see King's methods as more effective. ___
g3.why: 'On the other hand' introduces the opposing view in a balanced argument.

g4.label: 4. Both men wanted equality; ___
g4.why: After a semicolon, 'nevertheless' concedes the point and then contrasts it.

g5.label: 5. King organised marches and boycotts. ___
g5.why: 'Furthermore' adds another supporting point rather than contrasting.

g6.label: 6. ___ (sentence opener)
g6.why: 'While' opens a subordinate clause that contrasts with the main clause.

g7.label: 7. Malcolm X's approach was more radical. ___
g7.why: 'In contrast' begins a sentence setting one idea against the previous one.

g8.label: 8. Both leaders are honoured today ___
g8.why: 'Despite' is followed by a noun or -ing form, not a full clause.

g1.label: 1. laws keeping people apart
g1.why: Segregation is the legal separation of racial groups.

g2.label: 2. refusing to buy as protest
g2.why: A boycott withdraws custom from a business as a protest.

g3.label: 3. unfair treatment because of race
g3.why: Discrimination is treating people unfairly for who they are.

g4.label: 4. sitting and refusing to leave
g4.why: A sit-in occupies a place peacefully until demands are met.

g5.label: 5. same rights and opportunities
g5.why: Equality means everyone has the same rights and chances.

g6.label: 6. someone campaigning for change
g6.why: An activist campaigns actively for social or political change.

g7.label: 7. protesting without violence
g7.why: Nonviolent protest rejects the use of force.

g8.label: 8. a fundamental entitlement
g8.why: A right is an entitlement such as freedom of speech.
